summary: Read-only: completeness-critic (what did the audits/authoring miss?), #27 Level-2 fusion-synthesis deep-design (beyond C0 MVP), and a production-scale (d2048/1B+) validation-harness design (RG6).

results.topic: Completeness-critic: gaps the 8-audit + 16-diff corpus MISSED or left unverified in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5
results.summary: I read the .perf/*.json audit corpus and the authored diffs, then spot-checked the live tree to find what the audits missed or asserted without checking. The headline finding: the authored BUG-INT32 fix (.perf/int64_offsets.diff) is broken on three counts — it does NOT git-apply to the live dispatch.cpp (context mismatch at :331/:236), it targets sm_90 files that do not exist (mega_transformer_decoder_adamw.cu, fused_megakernel.cuh, model_stages.cuh — the live JIT path uses mega_*_real_adamw_tc.cu + the *_megakernel.cuh headers), and it changes a function-arg `offsets` parameter that the live kernels pass as nullptr (dispatch.cpp:848) while the REAL int32 overflow source — `__device__ __constant__ int kDecOffsets/kVitOffsets/kMambaOffsets[]` (decoder_layout.cuh:50, vit_layout.cuh:65, mamba3_layout.cuh:73) and the codegen at megakernel_codegen.py:635/668 — is untouched. So BUG-INT32 is unfixed in the live H100 path. Second: a NEW int32 overflow the scale_correctness audit looked at but missed — the decoder embedding counting-sort (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:2469-2527) stores token-index VALUES and CSR cumulative counts in int32 (perm[], row_start[], acc, int T params); the audit cleared only the fence/memory-safety and the multiply-operand promotion, not the stored-value width. Third: opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh's re-inlined GRU/PEER math is the largest hand-written meta surface, is scanned by NO drift guard (check_math_single_source.py scans only opt_components.cuh + opt_stages_precompute.cuh), AND its B1 fp64 oracle mirrors the kernel (co-wrong) — three audits noted pieces but none named it as one actionable hole. Fourth: a stale-audit contradiction — megakernel_bug_hunt.json reports SG11-GATE-COS-OPERAND as CONFIRMED-live (parity_safe:false) but the live opt_stages_precompute.cuh:541-561 is already remediated (calls canonical sg11_sweep_a_step over momentum), matching optimizer_drift_audit. Fifth: the HIP/gfx942 and Pallas/TPU backends (shipped alternate-arch code, ~1700 .hip files) are essentially uncovered by all 8 audits. The fp64 A/A/A gate and the audits all center the H100 sm_90 JIT path; correctness regressions on the other two backends would not be caught.

findings.what: The authored BUG-INT32 fix (.perf/int64_offsets.diff) does NOT reach the live H100 path and does not even apply. `git apply --check` fails on csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp:331 (context mismatch — the diff was authored against a divergent copy with a `FusedScratch`/`float* v = m + n` layout the live file does not have). It targets csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_transformer_decoder_adamw.cu, mega_vit_adamw.cu, mega_mamba3_adamw.cu, fused_megakernel.cuh, model_stages.cuh — NONE of which exist in the live sm_90 tree (live uses mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu + fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh + model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh). The only change it makes to a live, used surface is the function-arg `const int* offsets` -> `const int64_t* offsets` in megakernel_codegen.py:210/281 — but the live decoder/mamba kernels pass /*offsets=*/nullptr (dispatch.cpp:848) and read the `__device__ __constant__ int kDecOffsets[]` table directly (decoder_layout.cuh:50, consumed at fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:255/284/1284). megakernel_codegen.py:635 STILL emits `__constant__ int kDecOffsets[]` and :668 STILL has the truncating `(int)acc` cast — both unchanged by the diff. The added check_total_params() helper is a non-binding warning nothing calls.
findings.why_it_matters: BUG-INT32-LAYOUT-OFFSETS (the medium-severity scale_correctness finding) is reported as fix-authored but is in fact UNFIXED for the production path: at any layout with >2.147B cumulative params the `__constant__ int` offset literals overflow (implementation-defined / negative), the `(int)acc` cast in offsets_consistent() wraps (false-pass or spurious build break), and `off = (int64_t)kDecOffsets[t]` faithfully propagates the wrapped negative value into the kernel address arithmetic. The fp64 gate runs at ~101M params and cannot exercise it. The ledger likely records this as shipped/handled when it is not.
findings.action: Re-author the fix against the REAL surface: (1) megakernel_codegen.py emit `__device__ __constant__ int64_t kDecOffsets[]` (and Vit/Mamba) — offsets only; sizes may stay int. (2) Change offsets_consistent() :668 `kOffsets[i] != (int)acc` to `!= acc` (drop the truncating cast). (3) Regenerate the three layout headers so the live `__constant__` tables become int64_t. (4) Confirm `(int64_t)kDecOffsets[t]` casts at the consume sites still typecheck. (5) Discard/rewrite int64_offsets.diff — it does not apply and edits nonexistent files. Add a codegen-time `assert total < (1<<31)` OR go unconditionally int64 so the guard cannot drift again.

findings.what: NEW int32 overflow the scale_correctness audit examined but missed: the decoder embedding counting-sort. dectc_embed_build_lists (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:2469-2527) and dectc_embed_owner_scan (:2532) take `int T`, store token-index VALUES in `int* perm` via `perm[cur[r]++] = t` (:2523) where t reaches T-1, accumulate CSR counts in `int acc`/`int* row_start` (:2493-2498), and the scratch is carved as `int* embed_perm` (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:779-780). The launcher truncates `const int B = (int)targets.numel()` (mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu:93), so T=B*kSeq is an int32 throughout the embed path.
findings.why_it_matters: scale_correctness_audit cleared this exact code in its INVESTIGATED-AND-CLEARED items #4 (fence/memory-safety only) and #5 (it reasoned 'T stays int32 but is bounded by T which only overflows at unrealistic B>536M' — treating T solely as a loop bound / multiply operand, NOT as a stored VALUE). But perm[] stores per-token indices and row_start/acc store cumulative token counts; both overflow int32 at T>2.147B tokens (a 1B+-param decoder at long sequence/large batch reaches this well before the audit's 536M figure, which assumed kSeq=4). On overflow the embedding gradient is silently corrupted (negative/wrapped indices into perm or grad), with no gate able to catch it (gate runs the toy p=97 scale).
findings.action: Widen the embed path to int64: change dectc_embed_build_lists/dectc_embed_owner_scan signatures to `int64_t T`, make row_start/perm/acc/cursors int64_t (carve embed_perm as int64_t* in fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:780 and bump dec_embed_lists_floats to 2 float-slots per int64 entry), and keep B as int64_t at the launcher. Same >2.1B threshold as BUG-INT32; bundle the two int64 widenings into one scale-hardening pass and add a scaled (non-gate) static assertion.

findings.what: opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh's re-inlined GRU (S3) + PEER (S4) math is the largest hand-written optimizer meta-net surface and is guarded by NOTHING. The header itself admits S3/S4 are 'hand-written sequential dot products + expf/tanhf' rather than calls to canonical algo:: fns (opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:136-141), while CSA/HCA call canonical sg11-style fns. The live drift guard check_math_single_source.py scans ONLY opt_components.cuh (_consumer_headers :254) and opt_stages_precompute.cuh (_cosine_consumer_headers :226), and explicitly excludes supergrok2 via SG2_SEPARATE_PATH (:301,:313). Separately, SG2's B1 fp64 oracle (tests/hw/sg2_kernel_mirror.py::oracle_step:356-391) MIRRORS the kernel's low-rank indexer instead of the canonical full-rank path (oracle_trust_audit's first co_wrong finding), and the only instrument that would catch full-rank divergence (the N>64 fidelity probe, _sg2_l3tc_gate.py:320-333) is non-voting (prints under `if verbose`, sets no _ok flag).
findings.why_it_matters: Three separate audits each touched one facet (optimizer_drift gap-D: SG2 unscanned; oracle_trust: SG2 oracle co-wrong; the low-rank-vs-full-rank divergence is non-voting) but none stated the combined hole: a drift in SG2's GRU gate order (z/r swap), PEER softmax temperature, or indexer projection would pass the drift guard (doesn't scan it), pass B1 parity (oracle mirrors the kernel), and pass the gate verdict (the discriminating probe doesn't vote). SG2 is one of the headline meta-optimizers; its heaviest math is the least-guarded.
findings.action: (1) Add opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh to BOTH _consumer_headers() and _cosine_consumer_headers() in check_math_single_source.py and route S3/S4 through canonical algo:: GRU/PEER fns (single-source them). (2) Make oracle_step compute the indexer top-k via the CANONICAL full-rank path (qI=(x@idx_DQ)@idx_UQ, /sqrt(d)) per supergrok2.py:449-450, and (3) make the N>64 fidelity probe set an _ok flag that participates in `ok = b1_ok and aaa_ok and tie_ok` (_sg2_l3tc_gate.py:335) under a justified tolerance.

findings.what: Stale-audit contradiction on SG11. megakernel_bug_hunt.json reports SG11-GATE-COS-OPERAND as CONFIRMED-live with parity_safe:false (claims the staged gate computes cos(grad,MU) with a helper that 'has NO momentum parameter at all'). The live tree contradicts this: opt_stages_precompute.cuh:541-561 calls `algo::sg11_sweep_a_step(mu_blob, grad, sharpness, momentum, mu_val, gi, num, den_g, den_m)` reducing over momentum (= st.exp_avg start-of-step), and finalizes via algo::sg11_finalize_gate — i.e. already remediated, exactly as optimizer_drift_audit.json reports (severity 'none-now (remediated)').
findings.why_it_matters: The two JSONs disagree on whether a HIGH-severity correctness bug is live. A reader consuming megakernel_bug_hunt.json in isolation (or a future agent diffing it) would re-chase a non-bug or, worse, 'fix' the already-correct momentum operand back to mu. The bug_hunt corpus appears to predate the SG11 fix and was never re-anchored. The genuinely-live residual is NOT the operand (fixed) but the gate blindness: the fp64 oracle still mirrors the kernel and the warm-up discriminator is not pytest-collected (see MISS-5).
findings.action: Annotate megakernel_bug_hunt.json's SG11-GATE-COS-OPERAND entry as HISTORICAL/remediated (point to opt_stages_precompute.cuh:547 + sg11_gate_fix.diff) so it reconciles with optimizer_drift_audit, and carry forward ONLY the still-live gate-blindness residual.

findings.what: The SG11/SG15 momentum-divergence warm-up gate — the test written specifically to catch the SG11 cos-operand class — is STILL not collected by pytest in the live tree. The only @pytest.mark.hw test is test_l3tc_cell_gate (test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:1457-1460) running the COLD step-1 path (the file's own docstring at :884-887 admits step-1 is blind: m=v=0 so cos(grad,mu)==cos(grad,momentum)). run_sg11_warmup_gate (:882) is reachable ONLY via the --sg11-warmup CLI flag (:1479-1494); CI runs plain `pytest tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py -m hw` (ci.yml:1353) which never passes it. There is still no `def test_sg11_gate_warmup_catches_momentum_bug` (the docstring at :691 advertises it). SG15 is worse — run_sg11_warmup_gate hard-asserts opt=='supergrok11' (:904), so the 3 SG15 cells have no warm-momentum gate at all.
findings.why_it_matters: This is flagged by oracle_trust_audit and test_coverage_gap_audit (RG1) but is NOT closed in the live tree — confirming it is still an open hole, not a remediated one. The exact regression class that bit SG11 (and could bite SG15, which shares the staged mu/cosine machinery) has no CI-running guard.
findings.action: Add `@pytest.mark.hw @pytest.mark.parametrize('cell', supergrok11_cells) def test_sg11_warmup_gate_<cell>` wrapping run_sg11_warmup_gate (asserts ok ∧ gate_div>1e-4 ∧ mom_norm≫0, skips cleanly off-GPU), generalize the :904 SG11-only assert to an SG15 analog, and de-mirror the fp64 oracle (compute cos(grad,exp_avg) from first principles, warmed-up multi-step) so step-1 coincidence cannot fake-green it.

findings.what: The HIP/gfx942 backend (~all of csrc/backends/hip/gfx942/* + csrc/fused/gfx942/* + grokking_optimizers/kernels/gfx942/* — the MFMA/DPP/FP8 device kernels, 33 mega_*.hip cells, the attention path device_attention.hip, the launchers) and the Pallas/TPU-v6e backend (csrc/backends/pallas/* + csrc/fused/tpu_v6e/*) are essentially uncovered by all 8 audits. Only needs_care_unblock_plan touches HIP (dead-weight removal of mma.cuh/CUTLASS), and the int64_offsets.diff edits the gfx942 mega files — but no audit verifies gfx942/Pallas correctness, math-single-source, or parity against the CUDA path. setup.py builds the full HIP tree under _is_hip (lines 498-575), so this is shipped code, not dead.
findings.why_it_matters: The fp64 A/A/A gate, check_math_single_source.py, and every audit center the H100 sm_90 JIT path. The HIP and Pallas backends carry their own re-implementations of the 11 optimizers + 3 models (a second and third copy of the canonical math). A drift between csrc/algorithms/*.h and the gfx942/Pallas kernels — or an SG11-class wrong-operand in device_supergrok11.hip / launch_supergrok11.py — has no gate and was never audited. If MI300X/TPU is a real target, this is a large unverified correctness surface.
findings.action: Scope a HIP/Pallas parity audit: (1) confirm whether gfx942/v6e are live targets or aspirational (if dead, document + exclude from build to stop the int64-style stale-diff churn); (2) if live, extend check_math_single_source.py to scan the gfx942/Pallas optimizer kernels for re-inlined canonical math, and add a CPU/numpy fp64 parity gate for at least the SG-tier optimizers on those backends; (3) reconcile that int64_offsets.diff edits gfx942 mega files for a fix that the sm_90 path needs but does not actually receive.

findings.what: Four deliverables. 1 emit_fragment_source emits a device functor as the Out param of the unchanged tc_gemm_block_unpipelined engine, reusing the elementwise affine core at 30019 but suppressing the global wrapper and the extern C host launcher, output a cuh; whole TU emitters are C2 illegal in the persistent megakernel. 2 the fusion pattern library has three tiers: byte identical r1 and r2 residual bias and FUSE_B ff0 gelu are the emitter target; FOLD A qkv bias single vs double round is needs parity gate arbitrated; the LN residual resident fold and any reduce node are forbidden and rejected at emit. 3 the search reuses ifndef SG_TUNED auto knob discovery pinned OFF, the pick_winner ratchet, and the keying fixed swap, with a new ORIGIN_FUSION origin and independent fold knobs. 4 the per candidate gate must rebuild gated ops with the fold macro and fragment then run the cell gate in a fresh subprocess, since the fp64 hook today gates a stale memoized ops singleton; add an occupancy pre gate.
findings.why_it_matters: The chain is already hand authored in c0_r1fold_mvp.diff and decoder_p1_fusion.diff, so the emitter only has to reproduce known good fragments byte for byte by PTX diff, not invent fusions; this collapses the feasibility risk and makes most of Phase C CPU verifiable. Without the subprocess gate and the keying fix stash 14643 vs read 17852 Phase C ships fake green.
findings.action: C0.0 first: fix keying with a self test and re architect the decoupled hook. Then C1 emitter with a body diff versus the hand SynthEpiR1, C2 the seam PTX byte identical OFF path in model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh, C3 the subprocess gate with a negative self test, C4 sweep R1 keep if faster three seeds and parity clean at d2048. Gate ViT and Mamba on the decoder verdict; record each on the P series ratchet.

results.topic: RG6 d=2048 validation harness for the fused L3-TC megakernels

findings.what: New tuning/scale_gate.py. d=2048 already compiles (SG_DEC_BENCH_LAYOUT=1 decoder_layout.cuh:40); tc_train_step is a real in-place step returning loss,grad so AdamW runs today. STABILITY=200-step loop on a fixed batch (isfinite HARD-FAIL, grad-norm vs clip fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1140, loss down). DETERMINISM=full-run AAA 3x bit-identical (test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:1410) + ncta 0-vs-66 + B-tiling. SCALE-PARITY=d128 faithfulness prereq + apply-tail spot-check at d2048 + d512 ladder; no d2048 oracle (SG11 co-wrong shape).
findings.why_it_matters: First real multi-step d=2048 run; catches multi-CTA reduce/clip/fp32 bugs invisible to d=128 single-step.
findings.action: Author scale_gate.py; run decoder/vit AdamW seeds 42,7,123; other opts need an opt_id binding (launcher :199).

findings.what: THROUGHPUT reuses decoder_bench.py --profile --d 2048 + tuning.roofline. MAMBA BLOCKED: d=1024 OOMs ~199 GiB (BUG-04) + 668 GB reduce (PERF_ANALYSIS.md:68). RG4: hook compile.py:7213 claims d=2048 but runs d=128.
findings.why_it_matters: RG4 is the SG11 disease, so a d=128 hook ships a winner that breaks at d=2048.
findings.action: Fold throughput in; mamba=BLOCKED skip; repoint compile.py:7213 at d=2048.
